items.followUp: Why are gases more compressible than liquids?

rubric.why: Identifies the greater spacing between gas particles.
rubric.description: States that gas particles are much farther apart than particles in liquids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the large spaces between gas particles.

rubric.why: Links particle spacing to lower density.
rubric.description: Explains that a given volume of gas has less mass than the same volume of liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gases have fewer particles or less mass per unit volume.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in liquids, so there are fewer particles in a given volume.
Therefore, gases have less mass per unit volume and lower density than liquids.

items.followUp: What does m/v % mean for a solution?

rubric.why: Identifies the quantities and solution basis in the definition.
rubric.description: Defines V/m % as the volume of solute present in 100 g of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the volume of solute and the 100 g solution basis.

rubric.why: Gives the correct relationship for volume/mass percentage.
rubric.description: States the formula: volume of solute divided by mass of solution, multiplied by 100.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula or an equivalent statement of the ratio.

modelAnswer: V/m % is the volume of solute, in cm³, present in 100 g of solution.
V/m % = (volume of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100.

items.followUp: What happens to the concentration of a solution when more solvent is added?

rubric.why: Identifies how dilution is carried out.
rubric.description: States that dilution is carried out by adding solvent to a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the addition of solvent as the process of dilution.

rubric.why: Describes the effect of dilution on solute amount or concentration.
rubric.description: States that the amount of solute remains unchanged while the concentration decreases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the amount of solute remains unchanged or that the concentration decreases.

modelAnswer: Dilution is carried out by adding more solvent to a solution.
The amount of solute remains unchanged, but the concentration of the solution decreases.

items.followUp: Why does a solution, unlike a suspension, have a uniform composition?

rubric.why: Identifies the properties of suspension particles.
rubric.description: States that suspension particles do not dissolve or are relatively large.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that suspension particles remain undissolved or are relatively large.

rubric.why: Explains why a suspension is not homogeneous.
rubric.description: States that suspension particles are not uniformly distributed or may settle on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking uneven distribution or settling to the lack of homogeneity.

modelAnswer: The particles of a suspension do not dissolve and are relatively large.
They are not uniformly distributed and may settle on standing, so the suspension is not homogeneous.
